description: Writing quality guidelines — rules for evaluating the writing quality of finding sections. Sourced from EVVO SOPs and report style guides.

entries.title: Observation must describe the vulnerability clearly and specifically
entries.description: The observation section should clearly describe what the vulnerability is, where it was found, and how it manifests. Vague or template-like observations reduce the finding's usefulness for remediation.
conditions: observation does not describe specific behavior
entries.action: Flag as unclear observation. Suggest human rewrite with specific technical details.

entries.title: Evidence must be presented with clear request/response pairs
entries.description: Exploitation evidence should include clear HTTP request/response pairs, commands with output, or screenshots with annotations. Raw dumps without context are flagged as poorly presented evidence.
conditions: evidence is raw dump without context
entries.action: Flag as poorly presented evidence. This affects evidence_completeness but does not change classification by itself.

entries.title: Impact must describe specific consequences, not generic statements
entries.description: The impact section should describe what an attacker could specifically achieve (e.g., 'read arbitrary files from the server filesystem') rather than generic statements (e.g., 'could lead to unauthorized access').
conditions: impact uses template language like 'could lead to unauthorized access'
impact does not describe specific attacker capability
entries.action: Flag as generic impact. Reduce confidence. Do not auto-generate specific impact text.

entries.title: No placeholder or boilerplate text in any section
entries.description: Sections should not contain placeholder text (e.g., 'TBD', 'N/A', 'To be completed') or boilerplate that hasn't been customized for the specific finding. These indicate incomplete report writing.
conditions: text is boilerplate not customized for this finding
entries.action: Flag as placeholder/boilerplate text. Mark section as incomplete. Escalate for human completion.
